newsitem.title: GERMANY: TENNIS-SECOND SEED HUBER OUSTED BY OREMANS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SECOND SEED HUBER OUSTED BY OREMANS.

text.p: German second seed Anke Huber came down to earth with a bump on Thursday from her appearance in Sunday's Paris Open tennis final, losing 6-0 5-7 6-4 to Miriam Oremans in the second round of the Hanover Grand Prix.

The defeat was Huber's third in four clashes with the Dutchwoman, ranked 53 in the world. But the German, who received a first-round bye, said she had only herself to blame for an error-strewn performance.

"I just had a really awful day," said Huber, who lost in three hard-fought sets to Australian Open champion Martina Hingis of Switzerland in Paris last Sunday. "I completely slept through the first set."
Huber, who served 13 double faults during the match, appeared to have recovered her rhythm when she snatched the second set with a late break and went 2-0 up in the third.

But then Oremans took a four-minute break for treatment on a thigh strain, and Huber, the home favourite in the absence of world number one Steffi Graf, appeared to lose her concentration, ending the match with a double fault.

In a day of upsets, France's Sandrine Testud swept past Dutch fifth seed Brenda Schultz-McCarthy 6-4 6-3, and Anne-Gaelle Sidot, also of France, beat Belgian seventh seed Sabine Appelmans 6-3 4-6 7-5.
Yelena Likhovtseva of Russia, the eighth seed, restored a measure of order by beating Belgium's Dominique van Roost 6-1 6-2 to earn a quarter-final against top seed Jana Novotna.
